extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: researchers, naturalists, and informed scientific public (zoology, geology, archaeology, medicine)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical guidance for judging/presenting scientific monographs, expedition reports, and scholarly treatments (illustration, taxonomy, bibliography, methods, and interpretive caution). Aimed at reviewers, authors, and naturalists preparing or assessing such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: These are models of what such illustrations should be; admirably clear illustrations, reproduced from the author's drawings on eighteen plates, besides text-figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, faithful illustrations are essential to systematic works — they greatly enhance usability and value; a work without them would be much poorer. Reproduce author's drawings clearly and include sufficient plates/text-figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of figure labeling and correspondence with text
rubrics_metrics.description: Something wrong with Figs. 127 and 128 on pp. 855-6, the letters of the former not corresponding with the description, and the number of joints in the shaft ... not coinciding with the statement in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figure labels, lettering, and any enumerations correspond exactly to the textual descriptions; mismatches are blemishes (minor to specialists) but should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and correctness of bibliography and references
rubrics_metrics.description: This work does not include a bibliography, and such references as are given are not always to the point, e.g. Ann. des Sc. (6), 1899; the series should be (8) and the volume ix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monographs should include a full, accurate bibliography. Citations must be precise (series numbers, volumes, years) so readers can follow sources; incomplete or imprecise refs reduce scholarly utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative tables in taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Several comparative tables of the species of various genera are introduced ... This method of tabulation is the right one, and is capable of improvement until a degree of perfection is attained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tabulation to present distinctions between allied species — tables eliminate verbiage and banal verbal distinctions and provide a clearer, more useful comparative basis for future investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclatural restraint: avoid over-splitting species
rubrics_metrics.description: Two genera ... contain a multiplicity of specific forms which the authors admit may be only mutations. In view of this possibility, it is hard to accept so many names on an equal footing with those of undoubted and striking types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about naming many taxa when variation may represent mutation or intraspecific variability; require strong evidence before erecting species-level names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full bibliographies in monographs (completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full bibliography completes the present monograph, and one dealing with the littoral forms is promised later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete bibliographies (and promises to cover omitted but relevant areas) round out monographs and increase their long-term usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish general reflections from verified scientific theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The attainment of principles can only be by the long and fallible ways of observation, verified by the experimental method ... the danger ... lest we mistake mere generalities for laws, dialectic for analysis of origins, and axioms of provisional service for verified and permanent conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing broad reflections (e.g., 'Principia' style essays), clearly mark generalizations as provisional; do not present sweeping aphorisms as established laws without empirical/experimental verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge reflective works by the truth of their general point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: The author would be justified in answering that his reflections must be judged, not by items, but by the truth of the general point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating works of broad reflection, balance tolerance for minor factual slips against the overall coherence, insight, and truth of the central perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacology/therapeutics exposition: discuss timing, combinations, and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative incidence of remedies in time is dwelt upon, and the potentialities of combinations of drugs — a practice ... much neglected — are fully discussed, their mutual enhancements or cross-purposes considered, and an explanation given of the chemical room left in the body for additional drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good therapeutic writing treats temporal incidence of remedies, potential benefits and conflicts of drug combinations, interaction effects, and physiological capacity for additional agents (pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear definitions and practical limits for technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has introduced the salient facts both of sexual and asexual reproduction, but fails to offer a logical definition or a practical limitation of the terms spore, sporophore, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define technical terms clearly and set practical boundaries for their use so readers (and subsequent researchers) can apply concepts consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer introductions to new research lines and practical taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The author claims to have provided an introduction to new lines of research ... he has performed the additional service of discussing in a broad spirit their significance and interpretation; further, he has touched on most aspects ... and has outlined the taxonomy of the group with a view to practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable monographs both identify promising new research directions and give a practically useful taxonomic framework that others can build upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be realistic and effective in policy recommendations (biosecurity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless it is exceedingly drastic, legislation to prevent the introduction of plant diseases through imported plants and seeds would be useless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending legislative or policy measures (e.g., to prevent disease introduction), assess realistically whether proposed measures will be sufficiently stringent to achieve goals; weak measures may be ineffectual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement precautions and quantitative benchmarking in geochemical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: These results are obtained by measurement of the emanation, with every precaution against error. A sample ... contained sixteen times as much radium as the average of igneous rocks ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geochemical studies must report measurement procedures with precautions against error, provide quantitative comparisons to relevant averages or baselines, and discuss possible sources (e.g., extra-terrestrial input) and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validate plans and verbal instructions in antiquarian/archaeological sources
rubrics_metrics.description: All the old plans of a Gorsedd I have seen give 30° or so between the sunrise stones, and invariably the plans are contradicted by the verbal instructions accompanying them ... The writer ... did not quite understand the plans, but to his honesty as a copyist we are indebted for a very valuable document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing historical/archaeological documents, compare drawn plans with accompanying verbal instructions, seek and note contradictions, and value honest copies even if the copyist misunderstood; corroborate with independent archaeological evidence before asserting antiquity or function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-conscious restoration and over-interpretation of traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is over-consciousness in handling the bardic traditions that has worked havoc with them within the last century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise restraint when 'restoring' traditions or monuments; avoid inventing or over-systematizing material in a way that imposes modern coherence where none existed historically.
